spec_match.rationale: The demo follows the pinned WPT structure with a named timeline trigger, named animation trigger, finished-state exit, and re-entry observation.

interactive.rationale: Five controls drive the real native reset, entry, finish, exit, and re-entry sequence while exposing playState, currentTime, and playbackRate.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature index accurately describes the native runtime proof and its readouts.

edge_cases.rationale: Finished-forward re-entry is covered; reverse playback, repeated opposite actions, and reduced-motion behavior still deserve separate use cases.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus, the exact CSSWG play-action anchor, and the upstream WPT are directly linked.

conformance.rationale: The inherited suite remains visible and exposes its incorrect legacy view() assertion; it does not yet encode the runtime no-auto-rewind sequence.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chrome DevTools MCP in Chrome 150 exercised all five native controls at 390×844 and entry at 1280×800. Chrome 150 demonstrably restarted on re-entry, an honest pre-151 observation rather than a fake pass.

telemetry_health.rationale: The final native sequence emits a dedicated animation-trigger-no-auto-rewind assertion with playState and currentTime, without user content.

design_system.rationale: The demo uses shared variables, intrinsic grid sizing, a native scroll container, and reduced-motion handling.

accessibility.rationale: The scroll area and control group are named, buttons are native and at least 44px tall, and state changes have a polite textual live readout.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The lab uses one column at 390px and two at 1280px, with exact viewport widths and no clipped controls or document overflow.

openQuestions.title: Verify the passing sequence in Chrome 151 Android and desktop
openQuestions.detail: Chrome 150 correctly exposed the old behavior by restarting from 900ms to a running ~233ms state after re-entry. Record the same five-step MCP sequence in 151+ and confirm it remains finished at 900ms.

openQuestions.title: Build the complete action-state matrix
openQuestions.detail: Cover play, play-once, play-forwards, play-backwards, pause, reset, and replay across initial/running/paused/finished states from the specification table.

guidanceConsulted.query: Build an accessible scroll-driven animation trigger demo with live currentTime playState and reduced-motion support
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Prefer native CSS scroll-driven behavior, feature-detect exact syntax, respect reduced motion, and provide an honest fallback rather than a partial polyfill.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The lab uses native timeline-trigger and animation-trigger syntax, disables controls instead of simulating when unavailable, and reduces animation duration under prefers-reduced-motion.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: MCP observed native paused/running/finished states and Chrome 150's real pre-feature restart at both supported viewport classes.

guidanceConsulted.query: Expose live feature detection and conformance test results as an accessible educational details interface
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native controls, named regions, textual equivalents, and concise live status announcements.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Native buttons, a named focusable scroller, and a polite status readout expose all visual motion as text.

summary: A real native runtime lab now demonstrates the exact old-vs-new contract. Chrome 150 honestly restarts; Chrome 151+ verification remains the final browser-channel check.
